app.title: Sanitation and waste planner
app.tagline: From a town's excreta and waste flow diagrams to a plan. Bangladeshi municipalities.
banner.draft: Draft v0.2. Costs are placeholders that test the calculation. Do not quote any taka figure from this page.
banner.real: Draft v0.2. Option rules await expert review.
set.case: Cost case used to order options
set.hh_size: People per household, where none is stated
set.basis_stated: Stated in the SFD where given
outcome.lead_low: {safe} of excreta is safely managed. The rest reaches drains, water or open ground along four routes.
outcome.lead_high: With high groundwater risk no system in use here counts as contained, so {safe} is safely managed.
outcome.source_low: Source: SFD Lite, {date}, {by}. Shares of population.
outcome.source_high: The tool's reading of the SFD rules under high groundwater risk, not a re-run of the SFD.
comp.s11e: Septic tank effluent to drains or water
comp.w11c: Toilets discharging straight to drain, water or ground
comp.f15: Sludge sitting in systems that do not contain
binding.f11: {share} of excreta is emptied from pits and tanks and never reaches treatment. None of the 50 surveyed towns has a working treatment step.
binding.f15: {share} of excreta sits in tanks and pits that leak to drains, water or ground.
binding.w11c: {share} of excreta leaves toilets straight into drains, water or open ground.
binding.s11e: {share} of excreta leaves septic tanks as effluent into drains or water.
binding.fix_chain: What moves it: emptying, transport and treatment, together.
binding.fix_contain: What moves it: the containment options below.
binding.cost_contain_none: Costing: no costed option under this groundwater setting.
gap.lead: {persons} people in about {households} households use systems that do not contain.
sec.ranked: Containment options, cheapest per person first
ranked.lead: Ordered by yearly cost for each person moved from a system that does not contain to one that does. Figures show the mid case with the low and high case in brackets.
ranked.none_high: No costed option applies under high groundwater risk. The rule library offers a sealed, fully lined tank for pits and open-bottom tanks, and its cost row is empty.
ranked.none: No costed containment option applies in this town.
col.cpp: Per year per person newly contained, BDT
ranked.alt: Alternative for the same households as option {other}.
sum.title: If every household took the cheapest listed option
sum.covered: {persons} people in {households} households would move to a system that contains; about {safe} of them would count as safely managed at today's emptying habits.
sum.uncovered: {persons} people on {systems} have no costed option.
chain.lead: Emptying alone gains nothing: sludge moves from the pit to the environment. In SFD terms it turns safely managed excreta into unsafe. So emptying is costed only as a package with transport and treatment.
chain.untreated: {persons} people's worth of excreta ({share}) is emptied and not treated today.
chain.emptying_cost: Scheduled emptying on its own would cost a household BDT {mid} a year ({low} to {high}).
other.lead: These are in the rule library and cannot be ordered yet.
why.needs_treatment: Emptying needs treatment to count. See the package above.
why.not_applicable_gw: Does not apply at this groundwater setting.
why.no_effect_model: The tool has no rule yet for what this changes.
why.no_gain: Households are already on a system that contains.
peers.lead: Each dot is a town. The line marks the median.
peer.not_contained: People on systems that do not contain
peer.flips_if_gw_high: People on systems that stop containing at high groundwater
peers.rank: {value}. Higher than {below} of the other {n} towns.
sec.notes: What this draft cannot tell you
note.sfd_draft: The SFD is level {level}, status {status}. It rests on a household survey and officials' estimates, not on measured flows.
note.treatment_not_costed: Treatment is not costed. The treatment plant, vehicles and land have no cost data or sizing rule yet.
note.municipal_not_estimated: Municipal cost is not yet estimated. Every costed option on this page is paid by households.
note.systems_without_option: No costed option exists for {persons} people on: {systems}.
note.households_assumed: Households are population ÷ {size}; this town has no stated household count in the tool. In Kaliakair that assumption gave 19% too few households.
note.gw_assumed_low: The SFD assumes low groundwater risk and the tool holds no groundwater or flood data for this town. {share} of people use soak pits or open-bottom pits and tanks, which stop containing if the risk is high. Switch the setting to see that case.
note.gw_high_reading: The high-groundwater view applies the SFD's containment rules to the same households. It is not a new SFD.
note.safe_gain_assumption: "Safely managed" after an option assumes households empty as often as today's users of that system in this town.
note.conditions_unchecked: Conditions such as plot space, road access and density are listed, not checked. Not every household on a system can take the option.
note.draft_rules: Option rules are a first draft awaiting expert review.
foot.versions: Tool v0.2 draft. Rules and costs v{rules}. Town data v{data} ({source}).
foot.licence: Code MIT. Rules, costs and data CC BY 4.0. Town data: 50-municipality SFD and WFD study, aggregates only.
foot.privacy: Everything is calculated in your browser. Nothing you enter leaves your device.
error.load: The data files could not be loaded. Reload the page; if you opened the file directly from disk, serve the folder over HTTP instead.
banner.user_costs: Cost items changed in this browser: {n}. These figures are the user's, not the tool's, and have not been checked.
banner.typed: This town was typed in or read from an uploaded report in this browser. The tool has not checked the figures.

hero.san_all: Almost nobody's excreta in {town} is safely managed.
hero.san_none: Almost all excreta in {town} is safely managed.
hero.san_load: {share} of the town's excreta, from about {persons} people, reaches drains, water or open ground untreated: roughly {tonnes} tonnes of faeces every day.
hero.bench: Bangladesh as a whole: {value} of people have safely managed sanitation ({year}). {town}'s diagram: {safe} of excreta safely managed. The two are measured differently.
hero.waste: Every day about {kg} kg of plastic from {town} reaches rivers, canals and ponds.
hero.waste_small: {tonnes} tonnes of plastic a year escape the waste system in {town}.
hero.waste_fig: Where {tonnes} tonnes of escaped plastic end up each year
hero.waste_load: {tonnes} tonnes of plastic a year escape the waste system, {share} of all plastic waste. {collected} of the town's waste is collected; {day} tonnes a day are not.
hero.waste_missing: No solid-waste figures for this town. Add them under Your town.
first.more: See the full plan and try a target
dec.empty: Nothing in this town's figures calls for a decision here.
dec.treat.title: Build sludge treatment before buying more emptying
dec.treat.why: {share} of the town's excreta, about {persons} people's worth, is emptied from pits and tanks and dumped untreated. More emptying without a treatment plant moves more sludge into drains.
dec.contain.title: {option}: about {households} households
dec.contain.why: {persons} people ({share}) use: {labels}. These leak to drains, water or ground.
dec.no_option.title: Find a fix for {persons} people with no costed option
dec.no_option.why: They are on systems {systems}. The rule library has no costed option for them yet.
dec.no_option_gw.title: No costed fix under high groundwater: {persons} people
dec.no_option_gw.why: With a high water table, pits and soak pits stop containing ({systems}). The sealed-tank option has no cost yet, and septic tanks and direct discharge have no high-groundwater option at all.
dec.check_gw.title: Test groundwater before promoting pits and soak pits
dec.check_gw.why: {share} of people rely on soak pits or open-bottom pits and tanks. These stop containing where the water table is high or the area floods. The diagram assumed low risk without data.
dec.collect.title: Extend waste collection first
dec.collect.why: {collected} of waste is collected. The {tonnes} tonnes a day that nobody collects are the source of {share} of the plastic that escapes.
dec.dumpsite.title: Bring the dumpsite under control
dec.dumpsite.why: {controlled} of the {tonnes} tonnes disposed each year goes to a controlled site. Disposal accounts for {share} of the plastic that escapes.
dec.organics.title: Treat organic waste separately
dec.organics.why: {share} of the waste is organic: about {tonnes} tonnes a day. Composting it would cut what has to be hauled and dumped.
dec.handling.title: Stop plastic escaping during collection and transport
dec.handling.why: {share} of the plastic that escapes is lost from bins, loading and uncovered vehicles.
dec.cost.placeholder: Cost: placeholder figures; see the Sanitation tab.
conseq.title: What this loss means
conseq.load: The excreta of about {persons} people takes this route: roughly {tonnes} tonnes of faeces a day.
conseq.health: Unsafe water, sanitation and hygiene were linked to about {rate} deaths per 100,000 people in Bangladesh in {year}. No method turns one town's flows into a local death count, so none is shown.
conseq.return: A global study put the return on basic sanitation at about {bcr} for each 1 spent. It was not estimated for sludge treatment or for this town.
conseq.reuse: Treated sludge can be co-composted and sold as soil conditioner. Tonnage and value are not estimated: the yield and sale price are not in the cost sheet yet.
stages.lead: Largest source: {stage}, {share} of the plastic that escapes.
fates.lead: About {kg} kg of plastic reaches water every day.
waste.flag: The stage shares in this town's source file add up to {sum}, not 100%. Treat the split by stage with caution.
bin.lead: {organic} of the waste is organic: about {tonnes} tonnes a day.
swm.lead: Listed, not ordered: none has a cost yet.
waste.source_typed: Source: figures typed in or read from an uploaded WFD report.
plan.lead: Largest loss first. Each line says what to do, why, and whether it has a cost yet.
wi.san.lead: Move the sliders, or set a target, to see the town change.
wi.san.uptake: Households on leaking systems that take the cheapest fix
wi.san.target: Or set a target: % safely managed
wi.san.nochange: Move a slider to see the change.
wi.san.head: Safely managed: {before} today, {after} with these changes
wi.san.people: The excreta of {persons} more people is safely managed.
wi.san.no_option: No costed containment option applies at this groundwater setting, so the first slider changes nothing.
wi.san.treated: Sludge from about {persons} people is treated instead of dumped.
wi.san.cost_contain: Containment, paid by households: BDT {mid} million upfront ({low} to {high}), or BDT {amid} million a year.
wi.san.cost_treat: Treatment: see the package on the Sanitation tab.
wi.san.cost_treat_none: Treatment plant, vehicles and land: not yet estimated.
wi.san.basis: Assumes households that change system empty as often as today's users of the new system in this town, and that treated sludge counts as safely managed.
ways.contain_level: {level} of households on leaking systems fixed
ways.cannot: Cannot reach the target alone; tops out at {max}
ways.already: The town is already at {today}, above the {target} target.
wi.waste.lead: Raise collection or control the dumpsite to see how much less plastic escapes.
wi.waste.ctl: Disposed waste going to a controlled site
wi.waste.head: Plastic escaping: {before} tonnes a year today, {after} with these changes
wi.waste.unc: Waste left uncollected: {before} tonnes a day today, {after} with these changes.
wi.waste.cost: Collection, transport and disposal: not yet estimated.
wi.waste.basis: A proportional reading of the published WFD result, not a re-run of the WFD tool. Newly collected plastic is assumed to leak at today's rate along collection, transport and disposal. Where the plastic ends up is not re-estimated.
costs.lead: Change any figure and every tab uses it at once. Your figures stay in this browser tab; save them to a file to use them again.
costs.save: Save my figures to a file
costs.note: Prices in taka. One-off items are spread over their lifespan at the discount rate; per-service items are multiplied by times a year. An option is ordered only when every item it needs has a figure.
costs.loaded: Loaded {n} cost figures from the file.
costs.bad_file: That file is not a saved run from this tool.
peer.water_kg: Plastic reaching water, kg per person a year
all.lead: Choose a town to open it.
cmp.water: Plastic to water, kg per person
upload.lead: Choose a report PDF. The tool reads it in your browser and fills the form below. Check every figure before you use it.
upload.sfd_sub: DPHE CWIS-FSM Support Cell format, from the SFD portal
upload.wfd_sub: The case-study page saved with the browser's "Print to PDF"
up.failed: That file could not be read as a PDF. Type the figures in below.
up.too_big: That file is larger than 30 MB.
up.not_sfd: That does not look like an SFD Lite report in the DPHE format. Nothing was filled in; type the figures in below.
up.not_wfd: That does not look like a WFD Data Portal page. Nothing was filled in; type the figures in below.
up.sfd_short: The report's text gives shares that add up to {sum}, not 100%. {gap} of the population is on systems the text does not state. Find them in the report's SFD matrix (Table 2, an image) and add them below.
up.sfd_conflict: The report states more than one share for {codes}. Check them.
up.sfd_no_emptied: No emptied share was found for {codes}. They are left blank, which counts as 0%.
up.sfd_safe: The report states {safe} safely managed. Compare with the tool's figure after you press "Use this town".
up.sfd_no_factor: No sludge proportion for septic tanks was found. 100% is assumed until you change it.
up.wfd_read: Read {town}: unmanaged plastic {tonnes} tonnes a year. {version}
up.wfd_check_ok: The five stage figures add up to the total ({sum} tonnes).
up.wfd_check_bad: The stage figures add up to {sum} tonnes, not the stated {total}. Check them.
up.wfd_missing: Not found in the file: {fields}. Type them in.
own.lead: Type the figures from an SFD and, if you have one, a WFD. Shares are % of population.
own.name: Town name
own.total_short: Shares add up to {sum}%. {gap} points are missing.
own.total_over: Shares add up to {sum}%: {gap} points too many.
own.waste_lead: From a WFD report. Tonnes are per year unless stated. Leave blank to skip solid waste.
own.privacy: Nothing you type or upload leaves this browser. Close the tab and it is gone, unless you save a file from the Costs tab.
own.err.name: Give the town a name.
own.err.no_systems: Enter the share of population for at least one sanitation system.
own.err.share_sum: Shares add up to {sum}%. They must add up to between 99% and 101%.
own.err.wfd_missing: Solid waste needs at least: waste produced, % collected, plastic waste and unmanaged plastic. Fill those or leave all solid-waste boxes blank.
own.err.stage_sum: The five stage figures add up to {sum} tonnes, not the {total} tonnes of unmanaged plastic. The town was built; check the figures.
bench.lead: {town}'s diagram: {safe} of excreta safely managed. Bangladesh: {value} of people with safely managed sanitation ({year}). The national figure counts households with a service; the diagram follows the excreta. They are not the same measure.
bench.retrieved: Retrieved {date}. None of these is a town-level figure.
bench.wash_death_rate: Deaths linked to unsafe water, sanitation and hygiene
bench.faeces_g_cap_day: Faeces per person a day, used for the tonnes on this page
link.dphe_sub: City profiles on sanitation and solid waste. Not checked by this tool.
link.jmp_sub: The national sanitation ladder and its country file.
link.sfd_sub: Published excreta flow diagrams and reports.
link.wfd_sub: Published waste flow diagram case studies.
method.rank: Containment options are ordered by yearly cost per person moved to a system that contains.
method.chain: Emptying is never ordered on its own: without treatment it moves sludge from the pit to the environment. It is costed only as a package with transport and treatment.
method.whatif: The sanitation what-if moves households to the cheapest listed option and counts treated sludge as safely managed. It uses the town's own emptying habits.
method.waste: The solid-waste what-if scales the published WFD result. It is not a re-run of the WFD tool.
method.costs: An option with a missing cost or quantity is listed and never costed in part. Municipal cost with no data reads "not yet estimated", never 0.
method.pdf: The PDF carries no taka totals while costs are placeholders.
print.banner: Draft. For discussion, not for budgeting. No cost totals are shown: the tool's costs are placeholders.
print.waste_line: {msw} tonnes of waste a day; {collected} collected. {unmanaged} tonnes of plastic a year escape ({share} of plastic waste); {water} tonnes reach water. Largest source: {stage} ({stage_share}).
print.whatif_line: If {uptake} of households on leaking systems take the cheapest fix and {treat} of emptied sludge is treated: safely managed rises from {before} to {after}, the excreta of {persons} more people.
print.basis_pub: Based on the published SFD and WFD reports.
print.basis_up: Based on the uploaded SFD and WFD reports.
print.source: Sanitation: SFD Lite, {date}, {by}. Solid waste: Waste Flow Diagram, 50-town study.
print.foot: Sanitation and waste planner, draft v0.2, rules and costs v{rules}. Printed {date}.
note.sfd_typed: The sanitation figures were typed in or read from a report. The tool turned them into flows by the SFD Lite rules; it did not check them against the town.
dec.dumpsite.why_low: {controlled} of the {tonnes} tonnes disposed each year goes to a controlled site. This waste flow result puts little of the escaping plastic at the dumpsite ({share}), but it does not count plastic burnt there.
vs.lead: The tool holds its own waste flow result for a town of this name. Tonnes are per year.
vs.note: Where the two differ only at the dumpsite and in plastic burnt, the likely cause is the model version: the WFD Data Portal counts plastic burnt at the dumpsite as unmanaged and the study's files do not. This has not been confirmed with the tool's authors.
